metadata.title: Evaluate to true if the unix-def:file_test is properly supported
metadata.description: This definition is intended to evaluate to true if the interpreter properly supports the unix-def:file_test.

notes.note: It is important to note that the values used in this test definition are specific to a particular machine, and may not necessarily apply to your system. As a result, in order to have the definition return a result of 'true', you must either change these values to the ones found on your particular system, or you must configure your system to use these values.

criterion.comment: Test that the file test is supported with the path entity equal to a value and the filename entity is set to nil.
Test that the file test is supported with the path entity matching a regular expression and the filename entity is set to nil.
Test that the file test is supported with the path entity equal to a value and the filename entity equal to a value.
Test that the file test is supported with the path entity equal to a value and the filename entity matching a regular expression.
Test that the file test is supported with the path entity matching a regular expression and the filename entity matching a regular expression.
Test that the file test is supported with the max_depth behavior set to a limited depth of recursion.
Test that the file test is supported with the max_depth behavior set to an unlimited depth of recursion.
Test that the file test is supported with filepath entity equal to a value.
Test that the file test is supported with the filepath entity matching a regular expression.
Test that the file test is supported with filepath values supplied by a variable with operation 'pattern match'.
Test that the file test is supported with filepath values supplied by a variable with operation 'equals'.

file_test.comment: Expect 'true' with 3 items. Test that the file_object is supported with the path entity equal to /opt/support and the filename entity is set to nil.
Expect 'true' with 3 items. Test that the file_object is supported with the path entity matching some regular expression and the filename entity is set to nil.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with the path entity equal to some value and the filename entity equal to some value.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with the path entity equal to some value and the filename entity matching some regular expression.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with the path entity matching some regular expression and the filename entity matching some regular expression.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with the max_depth behavior set to a limited depth of recursion.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with the max_depth behavior set to an unlimited depth of recursion.
Expect 'true' with 1 item. Test that the file_object is supported with filepath entity equal to some value.
Expect 'true' with 4 items. Test that the file_object is supported with the filepath entity matching some regular expression.
Expect 'true' with 3 items matching var:1. Test filepath supplied by var:1 with operation 'pattern match'.
Expect 'true' with 3 items matching var:1. Test filepath supplied by var:1 with operation 'equals'.

file_object.comment: Retrieve a file_item with a path equal to '/opt/support/txt'.
Retrieve file_items with a path that matches the regular expression '^/opt/sup.ort/txt'.
Retrieve a file_item with a path that equals '/opt/support/txt/txtfile' and filename that equals 'build.win32.txt'.
Retrieve file_items with a path that equals '/opt/support/txt' and filename that matches the regular expression '^bu'.
Retrieve file_items with a path that matches the regular expression '^/opt/support/tx.$' and a filename that matches the regular expression '^bu'.
Retrieve a file_item with the path starting at '/opt/support/txt', recursing down 1 level, and filename that equals 'build.win32.txt'.
Retrieve a file_item with the path starting at '/opt/support', recursing down infinitely, and filename that equals 'build.win32.txt'.
Retrieve a file_item with the filepath equal to '/opt/support/txt/txtfile/build.win32.txt'.
Retrieve file_items with the filepath matching the regular expression '/opt/support/txt/txtfile/.+'.
Filepath fed multiple values via var:1 operation of 'pattern match'.
Filepath fed multiple values via var:1 operation of 'equals'.

file_state.comment: This state represents a file_item which has a path of '/opt/support'.
This state represents file_items which have a path that matches the regular expression '^/opt/sup.ort$'.
This state represents a file_item which has a path equal to '/opt/support/txt', a filename equal to 'build.win32.txt', and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents file_items which have a path equal to '/bin', a filename that matches the regular expression '^l', and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents file_items which have a path that matches the regular expression '^/opt/support/tx.', a filename that matches the regular expression '^t', and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents a file_item which has a path of '/opt/support/txt', a filename equal to 'build.win32.txt', and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents a file_item which has a path that equals '/etc/rc.d', a filename that equals 'rc', and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents a file_item which has a filepath equal to '/etc/profile', a path equal to '/etc', a filename equal to 'profile'.
This state represents a file_item with the filepath equal to '/opt/support/txt/txtfile/build.win32.txt'.
This state represents a file_item which has a filepath equal to '^/opt/support/txt/txtfile/.+, , and a size greater than '0'.
This state represents a file_item which has a path of '/opt/support'.
